_about: Tables for world/ENVIRONMENT.md. Climate numbers are modern climatology (the 1650 to 1730 Caribbean sat in the Little Ice Age: cooler and, 1645 to 1715, with far fewer hurricanes). Weather generation is a model. mark: rex | proposed | open.

climate.title: Caribbean monthly climatology (Kingston-type lowland station; modern normals)
climate.source: FAO regional description (trade winds 24 to 32 km/h from the east, 13 to 17 knots; Montserrat 24.7 C February low to 27.2 C July high); CIMH Caribbean climatology (SST 27 to 30 C, highest September to October); UK Met Office for Kingston (750 mm a year, February about 15 mm, October the wettest at about 130 mm); hurricane season June to November, peak mid-August to late October (NHC). ENV-FAO, ENV-CIMH, ENV-MET

period_climate.title: The period's climate: what was different in 1650 to 1730
period_climate.source: Hurricane frequency fell about 75% between 1645 and 1715 (the Maunder Minimum), from Spanish shipwreck records and Florida tree rings (Trouet et al. 2016, ENV-LIA); Bahamian blue-hole records show regional variation. Kentucky study: the Caribbean saw a lull in storms, epidemic disease and drought while Europe cooled (ENV-LIA2). A measured Caribbean temperature anomaly was not found; cooler by a fraction of a degree is the general Little Ice Age picture.

weather_states.source: A per-day Markov chain by month: each state has a stay probability and transitions; the effects are the keeper's placeholders. Wind and current set the ship's speed with PIRATE.md 5a's daily speed formula.

currents.title: Ocean currents the voyage loop uses
currents.source: Florida Current 1.8 m/s (about 3.5 knots) at its core, transport 30 Sv; the Caribbean Current reaches 60 to 70 cm/s (1.2 to 1.4 knots) along the Venezuelan, Colombian and Panamanian coasts, with a 1953 Navy survey reporting 'often exceeding one knot'; Antilles Current sluggish at the surface (about 10 cm/s); the Gulf Stream carries the Florida Current north then east. sun.title: Sun and daylight
sun.source: At 15 to 20 N day length runs from about 11 h (December) to 13 h (June); the sun is overhead twice a year; UV index at noon 11+ in summer (modern). Sunburn in untanned skin in 15 to 30 minutes at noon.
